title: Stop the audit log from recording saves that changed nothing

blocks.text: Every time a customer presses Save in the profile editor, the audit log lists the fields the save changed, and the customer gets a "your profile was updated" mail naming them. Since the editor was rewritten, the log lists fields that nobody touched, and saving a profile with its website cleared fails with an exception instead of being logged.
The stored values come from the database as `String`s. The editor hands over each submitted value as whatever `CharSequence` it keeps the text in. An empty field is `null`, on either side.

`ProfileAudit.changedFields(...)` already walks the fields. Finish the `TODO` in `changed(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ProfileAudit.java`: a field changed when its text is different, when it was empty and now has text, or when it had text and is now empty. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a field is reported when its submitted text differs from the stored text, including a field that was empty and is now filled in
a value the editor hands over in a StringBuilder counts as unchanged when it holds the stored text
a field that is empty before and after the save is not reported
clearing a field that had a value is reported, without an exception

origin.section: equals Is True Only for Another String, and Its Receiver Must Not Be null

concepts: String.equals is true only for another String with the same units, so a StringBuilder with the same text is never equal, Objects.equals included; contentEquals compares any CharSequence.
x.equals(y) throws when x is null while equals(null) is false; Objects.equals treats two nulls as equal.
